summary: PART A (baseline). TAOM's load-time numbers come from single runs on one machine. They are not a controlled series. The 11.9 s MissionInitialize to MissionAfterStartBegin gap (2026-08-07) was split on 2026-08-08 into: native InitializeMission 2 ms, async wait 903 ms (polls=28, healthy streaming), warm-up ticks 1,582 ms, other mods 846 ms and TAOM 55 ms. After that, 19.5 s passed after FinishMissionLoadingDone at memLoad 97%. The doc put that on memory pressure and never ran the clean-boot repeat. CORRECTION TO THE TASK PREMISE: 'resource residency is dead as a mechanism' comes from the #389 Isengard black-tableau investigation (CHANGELOG-2026-H2-handwritten.md:19172; rca-isengard-black-tableau-2026-08-06.md:174), not from battle loads. For its 2026-08-08 run, battle-load-diagnostics.md:783-787 concluded the opposite ('load time and memory pressure are ONE problem'). Later work (bundle b18f3441, 2026-09-04) showed that the window after FinishMissionLoadingDone can also be shader compilation (the render-ready gate, WaitingForRender phase 4f). That leaves the Aug-8 19.5 s, the Aug-8 21:50 33 s and the Aug-10 67.4 s (at memLoad 56%) without a split between the two causes. Fresh 2026-10-02 logs show loads of 1.9 to 2.9 s on a warm cache. Boot and first-load costs are explained and fixed: Native2Managed went from 29-33 s to 51-68 ms, PatchShield pass 2 from 69 s to 0.9-1.4 s, and the loading-window trace from 84 MB logs to under 0.4 MB. Frame time on record: 661 agents at 172-183 fps, 1,313 agents at 91-97 fps. Spawn spikes up to 1,663 ms and recurring single-frame hitches of 0.6 to 1.1 s have no attribution, and the warg fix (#659) has no frame-time measurement. Memory: the 6.6 GB menu floor is attributed (Armory about 970 MB, TAOM about 700, TAOM_Map about 500, the rest engine and vanilla). The map scene is about 4.4 GB, and about 3.1 GB of it moves with the engine's graphics sliders. About 3.9 GB of regions generated at load are still unnamed. PART B (repeatability). No TAOM Custom Battle preset exists, and no automated starter is in use. The parked shader-precompile walk already holds the machinery: a programmatic CustomBattleData builder plus a StartNewGame/EndGame chain driven from OnApplicationTick. No TAOM console command can run at the main menu. No parser for [MissionPerf] exists anywhere in tools/, and triage_battle_load.py reports only the last mission in a log. The 2026-10-02 session that loaded the same scene four times had 273, 83, 164 and 165 agents, so they were not the same battle, and steady fps on the same day differed 2x (about 117 against about 255) with no logged cause. PART C (native). TAOM is ahead on engine-method naming: 2,282 methods on 1.5.3, seeded into Ghidra. yotthani's 1.5.3 project has those names not yet applied, and his 1.4.8 project names 647 of them. Both binaries he analysed carry TAOM's project hash prefixes (client 45be32c5, wEditor 85c4d169), and TAOM's map puts GetMaximumNumberOfAgents at 0x6E4FA0, the address he reports. TAOM lacks callee trees, an offset-use search, an immediate-constant search, a function-size listing, range/enum/vtable-to-C decompiles and a committed struct-offset table. The smallest additions: native_decompile.py --callees, native_sig_author.py offsetuse and imm (capstone, grouped by .pdata function), a funcs --top size list, and a SHA-keyed native-struct-offsets.md. yotthani's Ghidra scripts are not in the MithrilForge repo, and docs/engine/native.md (2026-09-29) postdates TAOM's 91149e11 adoption cutoff, so /adopt-external fits it. BattlePresets has no licence, so it is comparison-only (provenance register row needed). /issue fits filing the additions. PROCESS NOTE: I ran one read-only `python -c` json.load on the engine-method JSON to list its keys. Python is outside the allowed command list. Nothing was written. Everything else used Read/Grep and allowed Bash commands.

instruments.name: [BattleLoad] load-phase ladder (BattleLoadDiagnostics, Patch43)
instruments.measures: seq + t=+ms per phase from EncounterStart/MissionOpenNew to BattlePlayable. Buckets: 1 native InitializeMission, 2 async IsLoadingFinished wait with polls=/waitMs=, 3a warm-up ticks, 3b Mission.AfterStart incl. AgentEquip burst, 3c OnMissionLoadingFinished; the triage tool also reports bucket4 = FinishMissionLoadingDone to BattlePlayable. Phase markers 4a-4f: MissionInitializeDone, MissionAfterStart, TaomBehaviors, FinishMissionLoadingBegin/Done, WaitingForRender (1 Hz, waitedMs + live shaders=). WaitingForSceneLoad heartbeat (silent under 3,000 ms, then every 5,000 ms). gc/heapMB/privMB/wsMB tokens on the key markers; per-agent AgentEquipBegin/Ok/AgentBuildDone

instruments.name: Battle-load stall watchdog + in-flight marker
instruments.measures: load window open past StallWatchdogSeconds (default 300 s, range 10-600): WATCHDOG line + crash bundle. Defers while the shader-compile count is moving (900 s continuous-compile cap). A surviving Logs/battle-load-inflight.marker signals a force-quit hang at the next launch

instruments.name: [BattleLoad] exit phases + [ExitStall] sampler (#331, #425)
instruments.measures: ExitBegin, ExitTeardown, ExitStateFinalize, ExitResourceClear, MapResumed, FirstMapTick, with GC/heap/isSaving. Main-thread managed stack samples at +15/+30/+60 s while a teardown is in flight

instruments.name: [MissionStall] battle-freeze sampler (Patch91, #634)
instruments.measures: stack of the agent-tick thread (Mission.TickAgentsAndTeamsImp) or the main mission frame (MissionState.TickMissionAux) when a tick is still in flight at 10/20/40 s

instruments.name: [MissionPerf] heartbeat
instruments.measures: every 5 s of wall clock in every mission: frames, fps, avgMs, p95Ms (nearest-rank over the newest 4,096 samples), maxMs, agents (AllAgents), active (Agents), live formations, gc0/gc1/gc2 deltas. MCM EnableMissionPerfHeartbeat, default on, re-read at 1 Hz

instruments.name: [MemSample] session memory telemetry (#386)

repeatableHarness.exists: Partial: protocols exist in prose and there are no tools for them. The mission-perf A/B rule is: from 30 s after F6 to the first rout, median avgMs/p95, three runs per cell (docs/features/mission-perf-heartbeat.md:64-68). The culture-doctrine A/B protocol and perf gate is: within 3% avg and 5% p95 at 800 v 800 (docs/features/culture-doctrine.md:523-585). The commit-matrix stations require the same scene, 250v250, the same cultures, season and time (docs/investigations/native-commit-audit-2026-08.md:348-351). Pieces that could be reused: the VS launch profile pins the module list (Main/Properties/launchSettings.json:3-10). taom.spawn_troops composes a fight inside an open mission (Main/Features/DevConsole/Cheats/MissionSpawnCheats.cs:27-45, at most 200 per call, ring around the player or camera :84-136). The PARKED shader-precompile walk is a working automated custom-battle starter. It builds CustomBattleData with a fixed scene, SeasonId 'spring', TimeOfDay 6f and fixed rosters, then calls CustomBattleHelper.StartGame (Main/Features/ShaderPrecompilation/TaomShaderGameManager.cs:48-69, 112-137). It chains MBGameManager.StartNewGame/EndGame per item from OnApplicationTick (ShaderPrecompileRunner.cs:14-40, :188), and its menu entry is commented out (Main/SubModule.cs:777-802). Several custom games in one process are safe (SubModule.cs:1556-1565).
repeatableHarness.gaps: 1) No battle preset: Main/Features/CustomBattles has no save/load of a setup (grep 'preset' finds nothing there). The 2026-10-02 'same scene x4' runs had 273/83/164/165 agents. 2) No TAOM console command can start a battle: all three TaomConsole gates refuse at the main menu (docs/features/dev-console.md:115-131). 3) No [MissionPerf] parser anywhere in tools/ (Grep 'MissionPerf' in tools: 0 hits), although Main/Features/MissionPerf/MissionPerfLine.cs:6-7 says 'the parser in tools/ has a single fixture to match'. 4) triage_battle_load.py scopes to the LAST mission only (tools/triage_battle_load.py:812-817), so N runs in one log yield one row. analyze_battle_logs.py is [AutoResolve] only. 5) No run marker, no auto-F6, no fixed camera, no auto-quit. The confounders are not logged: time scale, camera, AI control, deployment vs combat, window focus. Steady fps on 2026-10-02 differed ~117 vs ~255 between sessions with no recorded cause, and one session ran a .dirty build (BuildStamp MISMATCH). 6) No CPU sampler: spikes of 0.6-1.7 s are unattributed (lane-4.findings.md:101-104).
repeatableHarness.how: Today: launch with the managed-only 'Bannerlord' profile, keep engine_config and the [BattleSettings] options the same, pick the same Custom Battle scene, cultures, counts, season and time by hand, F6 on the first frame, then grep [MissionPerf] and run triage_battle_load.py --json per log. Smallest TAOM-owned additions: (a) tools/perf_runs.py, or a triage_battle_load.py --all-missions mode. It would emit one row per mission segment (scene, agents, buckets 1/2/3a/3b/3c/4, polls/waitMs, privMB) joined with that mission's [MissionPerf] steady-window medians and its [BattleSettings], [BuildStamp] and [Engine] tokens, plus a compare mode across logs. A twin literal test would pin MissionPerfLine.Build, the same C#/Python contract pattern [MemSample] uses. (b) A TAOM preset file plus a starter that reuses TaomShaderGameManager.BuildBattle. It would be reached from a main-menu option or a command-line switch read at OnBeforeInitialModuleScreenSetAsRoot, because the console cannot run at the menu. It would auto-F6 or spectate, end the mission after a fixed time, chain N runs with the ShaderPrecompileRunner state machine as template, and write a [PerfRun] preset=/run= marker for the parser to window on. (c) A one-shot context line per mission: time scale, camera mode, AI-controlled sides, graphics quality values. yotthani's HoN/BattlePresets is a reference design only: no licence (gh api repos/yotthani/bannerlord: license null), so comparison-only with a provenance-register row. Its design is an XML preset (Battle type/map/season/time/role; per-side troop id+count), an auto-saved last.xml, and a start via CustomBattleHelper.PrepareBattleData -> StartGame. It covers field and village battles only, at most 1000 per side, and has no spectator mode (README; Integration/BattleStarter.cs:14-16, 90-108).
